title: Reserved Capacity Contracts & Operational Controls PRD
creator: Liam Chen
summary: Define contract semantics, operator controls, and acceptance criteria for reserved capacity offers so tenants get predictable throughput while platform operators retain safe, auditable preemption and burst handling.
background: Customers have asked for clearer guarantees when they buy reserved capacity: what throughput is guaranteed, how burst works, how preemption behaves under load, and what actions operators can take without violating SLAs. Existing PRDs focus on allocator logic and fairness; this document centers the contract language, operator UX in Console, and observable enforcement points required for audits and SRE runbooks.
goals: Specify contract-level guarantees for reserved capacity (min throughput, headroom, burst allowances, and measurable SLOs)
Define preemption / soft-eviction modes with clear operator controls and rollback paths
Design Console surfaces for reservation lifecycle, credits ledger, and manual overrides
List telemetry and audit events necessary for billing, compliance, and incident postmortems
Provide acceptance criteria and test scenarios for deterministic fallback behavior
non_goals: Designing kernel-level scheduling or serving runtime micro-optimizations (handled by runtime team)
Pricing model changes (billing team will map contract semantics to SKU separately)
Full tenant isolation rewires for air-gapped on-prem installations (out of scope for this PRD)
requirements: Contract: able to declare in contract JSON: guaranteed_rps, burst_capacity_minutes, preemption_tier, headroom_percent
Operator controls: console actions to set emergency_reclaim, soft_preempt_threshold, grace_period_seconds
Fallback policies: deterministic per-tenant policy chain: reserved -> burst_pool -> shared_spill -> rate_limit
Observability: events for reservation_granted, reservation_reduced, preemption_started, preemption_completed, fallback_invoked, credit_delta
Audit trail: immutable entries with timestamp, actor, rationale, and revert_token for manual interventions
Safety: soft preemption must not drop existing in-flight requests below SLA targets for >=95% of requests when under normal degradation
Compatibility: new contract fields must be backward compatible with current reservation API (v1) and have a migration path
user_stories: As a platform SRE, I want to see which tenants are currently in soft_preempt so I can investigate if a large consumer is impacting others
As a customer, I want a clear guarantee of minimum concurrent requests and burst minutes so my product team can plan capacity
As an operator, I want a one-click emergency reclaim that records an audit entry and emits alerts to oncall
As a billing engineer, I want exact ledger deltas when burst capacity is consumed so invoices are reproducible
acceptance_criteria: Contract fields accepted by API and visible in Console reservation detail panel
When cluster pressure exceeds threshold, system triggers preemption_started events and applies configured preemption_tier in order
Fallback chain must route requests consistently: reserved -> burst -> shared_spill -> rate_limit; unit tests and e2e harness validate each hop
Console emergency_reclaim triggers an immutable audit row with actor, timestamp, and auto-generated revert_token

Soft preemption reduces new allocations but does not kill in-flight tokens; 95th percentile request latency for reserved tenants must remain within baseline + 2x degradation factor defined per contract
Burst minutes are consumed from per-tenant credit ledger and ledger entries are queryable via API within 30s of event
Rollout toggle exists (console + feature flag) and can be enabled cluster-by-cluster; rollback path validated by test harness
Security review signed-off and KMS key use for audit immutability verified
success_metrics: Reduction in capacity-related SEVs by 40% in first 3 months after rollout
<1% false-positive preemptions (cases where preemption triggered but not needed) after tuning
Customer-reported capacity incidents down by 30% for tenants with reserved contracts
Billing reconciliation discrepancies related to burst credits under 0.1% per invoicing period
rollout_strategy: Feature-flagged rollouts: staged on low-traffic zones for two weeks, then canary to 10% production traffic while monitoring preemption and credit ledger events; afterwards expand to remaining zones. Include manual hold points for compliance reviews.
monitoring_and_alerting: High-level: fraction of requests hitting fallback chain per minute
SRE alerts: preemption_rate > target over 5m and affected_reserved_tenants > threshold
Billing alerts: unexplained ledger drift > 0.05% over daily window
Security alerts: audit_entries_written < expected or KMS errors
operational_playbook_tasks: Runbook: steps to investigate a tenant entering hard_eviction after soft_preempt
Oncall checklist: when to escalate to product/billing/security
Manual rollback: use revert_token to restore reservation state and notify impacted customers
Periodic audits: daily job to verify ledger vs consumption metrics
open_questions: What exact SLA delta is acceptable for tenants under soft_preempt? (proposal: 2x tail latency multiplier or +200ms, whichever larger)
Should we expose an opt-in visibility field for tenants to view other tenants in the same burst pool?
How long should a revert_token be valid and who may use it?
Billing semantics: do we bill burst credit immediately on consumption or amortize usage over hour windows?
decision_log: 2026-03-03: Agreed to use a credits ledger (per-minute granularity) instead of immediate token decrement to simplify retries (decision: Liam Chen, Priya Singh)
2026-03-06: Chose soft_preempt semantics that stop new allocations but keep in-flight requests to avoid tail-killing (decision: Runtime lead: Marco Diaz)
2026-03-09: Require KMS-backed audit entries for manual operator actions (decision: Security: Rachel Park)
2026-03-10: Added Console emergency_reclaim with auto-generated revert_token and mandatory rationale field (decision: Product: Aisha Roberts)
engineering_notes: Runtime: implement hooks for preemption_tier and credit updates; provide deterministic emulator for e2e tests
Control plane: new contract fields validated at write time; migration path must fill defaults for older reservations
Console: reservation detail page must render credit ledger with pagination and filtering by event type
Telemetry: produce structured audit events to events.redwood-reservations topic with schema v2
notes_for_release: Include operator training session and updated runbook; schedule billing reconciliation job after week-1 data flush
